state.misconception_label: Confuses rest and movement on a distance time graph

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This graph shows how far Fido the dog is from his home. What might the negative-sloping section represent? ![A graph with time (secs) on the horizontal axis and distance (m) on the vertical axis. The graph starts at the origin, travels in a straight line up and right, travels horizontally, then travels in a straight line down and right back to the x-axis. ](). I got Fido has fallen asleep because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's revisit the concept of interpreting distance-time graphs. Remember, a negative slope on a distance-time graph doesn't necessarily mean that Fido has fallen asleep. Can you explain why the negative-sloping section might represent a different scenario based on our previous discussions?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: Um, so if the line is going down, does that mean Fido is getting closer to his home? Like, the distance is decreasing so he must be moving back towards home? But I'm still a bit confused about why that would be different from falling asleep...

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Let's clarify the misconception between rest and movement on a distance-time graph. Remember, a negative slope means the distance is decreasing, indicating movement towards the starting point. It doesn't necessarily imply Fido falling asleep. Can you think of any other scenarios where the distance might decrease on a distance-time graph?

score.justification_pass1: The teacher explicitly addresses the rest vs. movement misconception and the content is accurate, but provides too much direct explanation rather than eliciting reasoning, though the student does show clear improvement by Turn 2 in understanding that decreasing distance means movement toward home.
score.justification_pass2: The teacher uses questioning and prompting to elicit student reasoning rather than directly explaining the concept with worked examples as the traditional strategy prescribes.
